entries.subject: USGS global photographic mosaic
entries.finding: The 15,138 × 7,569 USGS Voyager/Galileo global mosaic supplies Monochrome on its roughly 1 km grid. Native detail ranges from 400 m to 60 km; the published Lunar-Lambert/overlap correction and exact-zero no-data are retained.

entries.subject: NASA/JPL/DLR PIA03456 via the official USGS RGBA release
entries.finding: The original 646 × 653 published plate supplies Galileo color, registered to the controlled monochrome mosaic using a frozen perspective camera and independent landmarks/quadrants. The 65° emission limit retains 28.735% of the sphere. These are processed display colors, not calibrated reflectance or natural-color reconstruction.

entries.subject: Galileo NIMS G8CNADLIND01A and G8CNGLOBAL02A
entries.finding: The registered Minnaert-corrected CIOF products supply partial Infrared color using same-parity bands near 0.77, 2.25 and 3.66 micrometres. Regional Asgard/Lindr coverage takes priority in overlap. USGS 2013 registered grids control geometry; missing cells remain missing. The view is neither natural color nor mineral abundance.

entries.subject: IAU/USGS Gazetteer centre-point export
entries.finding: Selected export supplies nomenclature labels, not terrain boundaries.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Lunar-like (Lommel-Seeliger) law of Squyres and Veverka (1981), which has no parameter. The Icarus paper is closed, but the authors' own summary in NASA's Reports of Planetary Geology Program 1980 (TM-82385, page 67) is open. It says Voyager clear-filter images at 10 to 124 degrees phase show that Ganymede's Cratered and Grooved Terrain and Callisto's Cratered Terrain are described closely by I = A F(alpha) mu0/(mu + mu0), and that bright craters follow it approximately. Flood-lit, this law is flat to the limb. F(alpha) is drawn in the report's Figure 1 and not printed, so frames with Shadows on carry no phase term. No emission range is printed; the limit 86.3 degrees is derived here from the outermost pixel of the finest clear-filter Voyager frame that holds the whole disc (Voyager 2 C2058321, 10.116 km per pixel) and is second class. Not used: USGS and the conference abstract on these mosaics (Becker et al. 2001) say they were normalized with a lunar-Lambert function with empirically derived values, which neither prints; Buratti (1991) fitted Hapke models to whole-hemisphere phase curves, which give no disc-resolved law. The Callisto photometry of Belgacem and colleagues covers regions only.
entries.revisitWhen: The paper's phase functions and emission range, or a newer global disc-resolved Callisto law, are read.

entries.subject: Shared sphere bank lighting (Lambert with a 0.35 flood floor and 0.05 ambient term, adapted from OpenSpace)
entries.finding: Replaced by the lunar-like law of Squyres and Veverka (1981); Callisto now bakes its own bank.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: NASA PIA00844 NIMS Callisto Global Mosaic (Galileo C3, 4 November 1996)
entries.finding: Only the left camera globe has a labelled graticule. The NIMS panel on the right is a disc picture with no grid and no color scale; the caption describes colors only as more or less ice. It adds nothing that can be registered beyond the included G8 NIMS observations.
entries.revisitWhen: The C3 NIMS cubes are mapped from the archive with their registration.
